title: POC scoping - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Echelon Logistics
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
summary: Discovery/POC scoping with Echelon Logistics to define success criteria, size the workload, and choose between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Customer cares about <50ms 99th percentile for short prompts, data residency in EU for some customers, and SOC2 audit logs. Plan: Redwood to run three benchmark scenarios, share security docs, and propose pricing + recommended deployment within one week.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and security pack (Jordan) - by 2026-06-12
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run with sample traces and dataset (Priya + Sara) - target 2026-06-16
Send draft pricing and Dedicated capacity options (Jordan) - by 2026-06-12
Set up trial API key and small hosted pilot for initial smoke tests (Luis) - by 2026-06-11
action_items: Jordan - Send SOC2, ISO docs and network diagrams - 2026-06-12
Priya - Prepare benchmark harness and test plan, include 1k qps synthetic test and 50 qps realistic trace - 2026-06-15
Sara - Provide representative request traces and sample prompt set (anonymized) - 2026-06-12
Dean - Confirm compliance stakeholders and timeline for decision (procurement/legal) - 2026-06-18
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining; uh, I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. we have Priya our se and Luis from solutions. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Mark: Doing well, thanks. excited to dig in.
[00:10] Dean: Hi, thanks for setting this up. We're primarily here to figure out what deployment mode makes sense for us and scope a POC.
[00:18] Jordan: Perfect. quick agenda — success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timeline, and then discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs. sound good?
[00:26] Sara: Yep that's exactly it. to add some color: we run a mix of short customer chat completions (~30-80 tokens) and longer document summarization jobs (1k-3k tokens), about 2,000 daily active sessions, peaks around 300 concurrent requests.
[00:40] Priya: OK, that's helpful. can you confirm p95/p99 latency goals? are you optimizing for cost or lowest latency?
[00:46] Mark: Ideally p95 under 150ms and p99 under 400ms for the short chat path. for the longer jobs we're OK with a few-second latency but want predictability. cost is important but reliability and data controls are higher priority because of enterprise SLAs.
[01:00] Priya: makes sense. on Redwood side, hosted api is fastest to get started — we can spin up a hosted pilot, you get immediate access. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools for predictable throughput and latency, and Private (VPC/on-prem) is for customers that need full control and data residency.
[01:15] Mark: For data residency, some of our EU accounts require that logs and any PII never leave EU. does Redwood hosted support region pinning?
[01:23] Jordan: Yes, we have regional hosted endpoints and can pin workload to EU region; however, audit/log retention policies differ between hosted and private. for full audit separation and customer-managed KMS we usually recommend Private.
[01:34] Dean: What's the rough cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
[01:37] Luis: ballpark, hosted is usage-based and typically lower up-front; dedicated is reserved capacity — you pay for the capacity (monthly commit) but get lower unit cost at scale and guaranteed SLOs. we'll send numbers but expect dedicated to be higher baseline cost but lower per-token cost at peak throughput.
[01:52] Priya: also dedicated helps with tail latency because of predictable batch sizing and no noisy neighbors; if you have steady traffic it's often the sweet spot.
[01:59] Sara: Our traffic is a bit spiky — weekly batch windows and daily peaks. we need autoscaling or burst capacity. how does Redwood handle that?
[02:06] Jordan: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity to hosted pools; Private can be configured with on-prem autoscaling but that depends on your infra. hosted auto-scales but you might see variance during big spikes.
[02:17] Mark: For the POC we want to run 3 benchmark scenarios: 1) short chat path at 50 qps sustained with 300 qps short bursts, measure p95/p99 and cost; 2) long summarization at 10 qps but 2-3k tokens; 3) mixed production trace with our real traffic replay. can Redwood run those?
[02:33] Priya: yes, we can. we'll need sample traces and a prompt set. priya continues: we'll run hosted first for baseline, then dedicated to compare tail latency and cost, and if residency or KMS needs force the private path we'll scope that.
[02:46] Sara: we'll provide anonymized traces and some sample dataset. are there any constraints on sending traces?
[02:50] Jordan: please remove PII and we can sign an NDA for anything sensitive; also we can accept hashed or tokenized payloads.
[02:58] Dean: Regarding security, we need SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC for teams, and KMS for encryption at rest. how mature are those?
[03:06] Luis: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, we support SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and for hosted we manage KMS but support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:19] Mark: Great. for the dedicated option, what's the minimum commit?
[03:23] Jordan: It depends on the GPU profiles and region. typical entry is a 4-GPU pool reserved monthly, but we can do lower for pilots or flexible burst arrangements. we'll include options in the pricing.
[03:32] Priya: quick technical note on benchmarking — we'll measure token throughput, end-to-end latency including network, and memory/kv cache behavior for multi-turn chat. for long docs we'll check memory pressure and whether quantization affects quality.
[03:44] Mark: Do you support quantized model variants and recommendations?
[03:47] Priya: yes, we have quantization profiles and compile-time kernel selection. we'll recommend a model/quantization combo based on your workload: short chat favors smaller low-latency models or optimized kernels; long docs may use larger models with chunking and streaming.
[03:59] Sara: What about model version pinning and rollouts? we need to be able to pin stable versions for production.
[04:04] Jordan: Absolutely, Dedicated and Private allow version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant on regression. hosted supports it too but with less isolation guarantees.
[04:15] Mark: For benchmarks, can we include 99th percentile targets and see the effect of batching? we want to know how batching impacts tail latency.
[04:21] Priya: we'll include both continual batching and no-batch modes; measure the tradeoffs. also include KV cache warm/cold scenarios because multi-turn chat benefits heavily from kv caching.
[04:32] Dean: Any gotchas around VPC peering or private deployments? network ops will want to know about NAT, egress, and maintenance windows.
[04:38] Luis: for Private we provide deployment guides; network team needs to allow specific IPs/subnets, we can integrate with your KMS or HSM, and we support a private control plane option. maintenance is scheduled with windows agreed on in the SLA.
[04:51] Mark: Ok timeline — ideally decision in 2-3 weeks. can you get us a recommended deployment and numbers within one week?
[04:57] Jordan: yes — plan: today we scope; by Friday we'll share security docs and pricing; next week we run benchmarks and deliver results with recommendation. that should let you decide within 2 weeks.
[05:07] Sara: who will run the benchmark and what's required from our side?
[05:10] Priya: we'll run the harness from Redwood. we need your traces, example prompts, and an account to push some test requests. if you prefer we can do a hosted run first to avoid any network complexity.
[05:21] Mark: We'll start with hosted baseline then compare dedicated. if the EU data residency or procurement pushes toward Private we'll scope that afterward.
[05:28] Dean: On procurement, we need contract language for data residency and indemnity. who handles legal?
[05:33] Jordan: Our legal team will work with yours; we'll include standard addenda for data residency and SOC2 controls.
[05:39] Sara: Any concerns about vendor lock-in if we go Dedicated or Private?
[05:42] Luis: We try to avoid lock-in — models and prompts portability depend on your stack. Dedicated and Private are more operational overhead but give you more control; we'll help with export tools and model artifacts.
[05:53] Mark: one more thing — we'd like to run a small LLM eval set for quality checks to ensure quantization doesn't regress. can you recommend an eval harness?
[05:59] Priya: yes, we have eval templates and can run A/B quality tests as part of the benchmark; we'll add that to the plan.
[06:06] Jordan: OK let's recap actions and owners. Jordan will send security and pricing. Priya will prepare the benchmark harness. Sara will share traces. Dean will coordinate procurement timeline. any other questions?
[06:20] Mark: no, that's it. thanks.
[06:22] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark run and a summary email.
[06:27] [end]
